To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) training multiple deep models with partially-shared parameters can lead to a performance degradation of previous models, (ii) we introduce a statistically justified weight plasticity loss to overcome multi-model forgetting, and (iii) we demonstrate that adding weight plasticity to neural architecture search improves the results of both computer vision and natural language processing tasks

(1) we observe a phenomenon of multi-model forgetting in which the performance of previously-learned models degrades as we train a subsequent one, (2) we introduce a weight plasticity loss to overcome this, (3) we demonstrate its effectiveness when learning two models sequentially, and (4) it is also effective in neural architecture search, which we demonstrate on natural language processing and image classification tasks

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the weight plasticity loss can effectively regularize the learning of the shared parameters of two or more deep neural networks that are trained sequentially, and can be used in neural architecture search to preserve the best models to be the final output.
we introduce weight plasticity to prevent multi-model forgetting, and apply the technique to neural architecture search.
we introduce a novel regularization term to prevent the forgetting of previously trained deep networks, which we refer as *weight plasticity loss*.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of a deep network can be improved by considering the performance of other deep models, which have been trained with the same parameters.

the training of a new model may degrade the performance of previously trained ones, and this can be mitigated by regularizing the learning of the shared parameters according to the performance degradation of previous models.
, when learning multiple models sequentially with partially-shared parameters, the performance of the previous models should not be ignored.
